display_name: Automated & Functional Test Suites (existing test code)

mcp_config.server_provider: Same GitHub/Git MCP server as application-code -- test code lives in the same repositories, this is a distinct manifest because it targets a different entity mapping, not a different transport
mcp_config.server_address_or_command: REPLACE: same as application-code connector, or a dedicated test-repo if tests live separately

entity_type_mapping.source_shape: Test file matching project test-path conventions (JUnit/TestNG/pytest/Playwright/etc.), AST/regex-parsed locally, deterministic
Test file or class grouping, e.g. a JUnit @Suite or pytest module
Test method carrying its project's configured traceability-ID indicator (v1.1.0: per-project, NOT a single global @TestId convention -- see project_test_id_conventions below)

project_test_id_conventions.$comment: REQ-METIS-CONN-06 (new, this revision): each project resolves its own traceability-indicator pattern -- there is no single platform-wide @TestId convention. Resolution order mirrors atlas-config-manager's existing pattern (project-level config first, host-level fallback, first-found-wins, no merge). Every entry below is a REPLACE placeholder -- none of these patterns are assumed to be real; they're the shape a project's entry takes, not a guess at your actual conventions.
resolution_order: project-level config file (e.g. .agents/configs/test-id-convention.json in that project's own repo)

if neither exists: connector halts ingestion for that project and surfaces a setup gap -- it does NOT fall back to guessing a pattern, per the same discipline as REQ-METIS-CONN-04's no-fabrication rule

per_project_entries.pattern: REPLACE: e.g. '@TestId\("([A-Z]+-\d+)"\)' for an annotation-style project, or '// TC-ID: (\S+)' for a comment-tag style project, or something else entirely -- this genuinely varies per project and must be confirmed per project, not assumed

temporal_strategy.t_recorded_source: Same as application-code: PR merge time primary, commit author-date secondary
temporal_strategy.known_pitfalls: A test file with NO match against its project's configured pattern must not have its Requirement link invented by similarity-matching test name to requirement text -- per CONST-014/RPI Forbidden Substitutions, an unmatched test is ingested as an orphan TestCase (feeding §7.2's gap detection directly) with confidence_tier=quarantine and a Requirement-link left null, never auto_write-tier guessed. This is the single most important rule in this manifest -- see notes. NEW pitfall this revision: applying one project's pattern to another project's tests (e.g. assuming @TestId everywhere) will systematically misclassify every test in projects that use a different convention as 'unannotated' -- this is worse than a random error, it's a correlated one that would make one or more entire projects look artificially orphan-heavy in DQ-019.

notes: REQ-METIS-CONN-04 (unchanged): explicit traceability-indicator presence is the ONLY basis for an auto_write-tier TestCase-to-Requirement link. Absent a match against that project's configured pattern, an LLM-assisted 'this test's name/content looks like it might verify Requirement X' suggestion is permitted ONLY as a quarantine-tier, human-reviewable proposal (confidence_tier=quarantine, tagged INFERRED per RPI's three-value scale, §9.2) -- never promoted without explicit human confirmation, since a fabricated traceability link is arguably worse than a correctly-flagged missing one (it produces false confidence in coverage, which is exactly DQ-017's core failure mode). REQ-METIS-CONN-06 (new): the pattern itself is per-project configuration, resolved the same way any other credential/config is resolved in this platform (project-level first, no cross-project assumption, no silent fallback to a guessed pattern).
